definition: A self-starter identifies and begins useful work without needing detailed instructions or repeated prompting.
entry_text: A self-starter identifies and begins useful work without needing detailed instructions or repeated prompting.
example: A new coordinator notices unanswered inquiries and creates a queue to track and route them.
label: Self-starter
sense_note: The label names a person characterized by initiative.

sources.note: Deterministic sample: first four SHA-256("worker-audit-v1:" + id) per populated non-language class, excluding null definitions and root-reviewed IDs; this is not a corpus accuracy estimate. Frese and Fay’s personal-initiative work supports the self-starting behavior; not a claim that the example measures aptitude.
